newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Anthrax threatens Australia dairy exports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Anthrax threatens Australia dairy exports.

text.p: Almost A$2.0 million worth of Australian dairy exports are threatened by an outbreak of anthrax disease in dairy herds in the state of Victoria.

The disease, a bacterial infection which causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats when they eat contaminated soil or feed, has been discovered in a minimum of 31 dairy herds in the Goulburn Valley, Victoria.
Australia is forecast to export A$1.8 billion worth of dairy products in 1996/97 (July-June), most to Japan, one of the world's most jittery markets.

An official with one of Japan's leading trading houses, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters on Wednesday that no impact had been felt yet on Australian dairy exports to Japan from the anthrax outbreak, which exploded in the last couple of days.
However, a rejection by Japanese importers of Australian dairy products would create a "virtually immediate" effect, he said.
The anthrax-affected area supplies about 30 percent of Australia's dairy products, while Victoria produces about 50 percent of the Australian total.
Most of Australia's dairy product exports to Japan are in the form of milk powder and other derivative dairy products, the trading house official said.
Anthrax infections were eliminated during the processing and posed no threat to consumers.
But it was feared the notoriously finicky Japanese market would generalise the threat Australia-wide and disregard the elimination of infection through processing, he said.

A similar psychology had caused major problems for Australian and other exporters of meat to Japan in the past year with Britain's "Mad Cow" disease and the E.Coli bacterial infection scare, trade sources noted.
Milk powders form 70 percent-80 percent of Australia's dairy product exports to Japan, worth almost A$310.0 million in 1995/96.

Australia's other main dairy product markets are the Philippines, which took almost A$240.0 million worth in 1995/96, Malaysia, which took A$150.0 million worth, and Thailand, which took A$147.0 million worth.
"The longer it goes on without any feedback from Tokyo the better," the trading house official said.
"(But) obviously Tokyo is quite anxious to see if the problem will have an overall effect on the market."
Already the anthrax outbreak already had been fairly well reported in the Japanese media, he said.
"We're more scared of the media than of anthrax itself," he said.

A total of 61 confirmed anthrax cattle deaths have occurred in an area between Tatura and Stanhope, Victoria. About 60 properties in the Goulburn Valley have been placed under quarantine because of the anthrax outbreak.
A meat industry worker has tested positive for anthrax in the Goulburn Valley and has been discharged from hospital.
The Victorian state government has stated that there has never been a link between treated milk products and anthrax.
Anthrax attacks lungs, causing pneumonia, or the skin, producing severe ulceration. If treated quickly it is said to be curable. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
